messages:
elaine: Quick follow-up on the atomic-pin + prefetch RFC — pairing session found two interesting races and a performance tradeoff we should decide on. Short thread with code + proposed fixes.

devin: TL;DR the repro you showed in staging — prefetch started, we returned early to the caller, then evictor reclaimed the page while the prefetch writeback/commit was still in flight. Result: transient stale-kv in the kvcache and a double-unpin path sometimes.

rohit: Yep. Root cause: our pin() currently only marks a soft reservation; prefetch is an async write/commit that upgrades to resident state. If evictor only checks resident it races.

maya: Two obvious options I sketched:
- Make pin() strongly synchronous (wait for commit) — simple correctness, obvious latency regression for cold requests.
- Make prefetch cancellable/abortable and teach the evictor to cancel inflight prefetches before reusing pages — more complex but keeps cold-path latency good.

elaine: I also prototyped a hybrid: pin() returns a light reservation token immediately; prefetch returns a Future and a cancel token. Evictor, on conflict, either waits for a short grace window (X ms) or issues cancel and reclaims depending on tenant SLAs. Pseudo API: ```
// reservation API
Res token = alloc.reserve_range(addr, len);
Future f = alloc.prefetch_async(addr, len, /*deadline_ms=*/50, /*cancel_token=*/token);
// evict path
if (!node.resident && node.reservation) {
   if (evictor.try_wait(token, 15ms)) { /* wait then recheck */ } else { alloc.cancel_prefetch(token); reclaim(); }
}
```

devin: That seems promising. Questions: what do we do for multi-page prefetch where some pages finish and others are canceled? How do we prevent partially committed descriptors in the kvcache?

rohit: We should enforce idempotent commit: prefetch commit must either publish all pages for request-id atomically or not publish any. Internally: write to staging area and swap pointer under a single atomic. That way cancel simply abandons staging.

maya: Right. That requires a small extra allocation per request (staging list) but keeps kvcache invariant clean. Also need a small lease timeout so abandoned staging is GC'd.

elaine: Performance notes from the pairing run: with a 15ms evictor wait + cancellable prefetch we saw tail p99 latency improve compared to sync pin (sync pin adds ~8-12ms on first token for cold requests). CPU overhead for cancel logic ~0.2% on our benchmark.

devin: Tradeoffs call:
- Synchronous pin (safe, simple): + correctness, - cold latency, - throughput impact under bursty prefetch.
- Cancellable prefetch + reservation token (complex): + keeps cold latency low, + flexible per-tenant policy, - more code surface and GC needed.

eli­ne (typo fixed): @ci-bot can you attach the small test harness we ran?

ci-bot: Attached: https://ci.internal/runs/atomic-pin-prefetch/456 (log snippet included) :white_check_mark:

rohit: Suggested decision: implement cancellable prefetch + reservation token, with a conservative default policy: evictor tries wait=10ms, then cancels. Expose config per-tenant and add an opt-in sync-pin for very latency-insensitive batch workloads.

maya: Action items:
- rohit: sketch safe staging/commit implementation (will include atomic publish + GC plan) — due EOD Thu
- devin: add unit tests for cancel edgecases + race harness + measure p99 delta — due next Tue
- elaine: update RFC with API examples and per-tenant config knobs — due Fri

devin: One more: add telemetry for "prefetch-cancel-rate" + "evictor-wait-hit" so we can tune defaults.

ess: Agreed. If no objections, we'll merge the prototype branch into feature/atomic-pin-prefetch and start code review tomorrow. :thumbsup:

rohit: No objections from me. :+1:

maya: Fine by me. I'll prep a small canary to validate behavior before rollout.

elaine: Thanks everyone — will open follow-up PRs and link here.
